parent_v7.key_result: restrictive same-source additions exactly protected robust impossibility, permissive same-source additions exactly protected robust reachability, while the opposite certificate types were vulnerable

scientific_question: As a compatible virtual-world universe grows one world at a time in random order, how long do robust reachability and robust-impossibility certificates survive, and how is certificate lifetime determined by the composition of the admitted world pool?

latent_rows.reuse: exact v7 eligible rows and the same frozen 25 percent dispersed positive-occurrence anchors
latent_rows.baseline_universe: v7 B0_reference surviving reference world for each baseline-compatible source
latent_rows.certificate_population: exact v7 unobserved locally A/B-permissive node population

growth_pools.restrictive_same_source: all compatible same-source worlds classified restrictive relative to their source reference world
growth_pools.permissive_same_source: all compatible same-source worlds classified permissive
growth_pools.directional_same_source: all compatible same-source restrictive plus permissive worlds
growth_pools.same_source_full: all compatible same-source worlds outside B0, including equivalent and incomparable worlds
growth_pools.all_source_full: all compatible worlds outside B0, including worlds from newly admitted sources

growth_process.sampling: uniform random permutation without replacement within the frozen growth pool
growth_process.exact_lifetime_calculation: for a baseline certificate with N candidate additions and K threatening additions that would destroy the certificate, expected first-failure draw is (N+1)/(K+1) when K>0; if K=0 the certificate survives the complete pool
growth_process.survival_probability_after_m_additions: choose(N-K,m)/choose(N,m) for m<=N-K, else 0; K=0 gives survival probability 1 for all m
growth_process.normalized_expected_lifetime: expected first-failure draw divided by N when K>0; 1.0 for certificates surviving the full pool
growth_process.fraction_to_draw_count: for reporting survival at fraction f, m = min(N, ceil(f*N)); when N=0, survival is 1.0

certificate_threat_definition.baseline_robust_reachable: an added world threatens the certificate when that node is unreachable in the added world
certificate_threat_definition.baseline_robust_impossible: an added world threatens the certificate when that node is reachable in the added world

primary_outputs: N and K for every baseline certificate under every growth pool
mean and median normalized expected lifetime for each certificate type and growth pool
survival probability at 10, 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent of pool growth
certificate type x growth-pool lifetime contrast
extra lifetime loss from incomparable/equivalent worlds
extra lifetime loss from new-source worlds

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every baseline robust-impossible certificate has K=0 under restrictive_same_source, and every baseline robust-reachable certificate has K=0 under permissive_same_source.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one baseline robust-reachable certificate has K>0 under restrictive_same_source and at least one baseline robust-impossible certificate has K>0 under permissive_same_source.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately if either vulnerability class is absent.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Under all_source_full growth, pooled mean normalized expected lifetime is strictly lower for robust-impossible than for robust-reachable certificates.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if impossible minus reachable mean normalized lifetime is >=0.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one certificate has lower normalized expected lifetime in same_source_full than in directional_same_source.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if equivalent/incomparable additions never reduce lifetime.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one certificate has lower normalized expected lifetime in all_source_full than in same_source_full.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if admitting new-source worlds never reduces lifetime.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every certificate and growth pool, exact survival probability is nonincreasing with the number of added worlds and endpoint survival at 100 percent equals the K=0 indicator.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every certificate and growth pool, the certificate persists after complete pool expansion if and only if K=0.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

secondary_outputs: certificate lifetime by truth barrier density, environmental autocorrelation and neighbourhood
relationship between baseline route redundancy and threat count
distribution of threatening-world classes for each certificate type
rows where a certificate survives same-source growth but fails after new-source admission
claim_boundary: World-growth lifetime is defined over random orderings of a frozen finite candidate pool, not calendar time.
Normalized lifetime is a robustness index, not ecological persistence probability.
Uniform random ordering is an experimental device for comparing candidate-pool composition.
The result remains conditional on the declared growth pool and occurrence evidence.
stop_rules: Do not change the growth pools after scoring.
Do not introduce weighted world-addition probabilities after scoring.
Do not replace exact combinatorial lifetime with a favorable simulated ordering.
Failed directional lifetime hypotheses remain failed.

preimplementation_amendment.reason: the frozen protocol named 10/25/50/75/100 percent survival outputs but had not fixed the integer draw-count rule
